phases.title: Phase 2h: Findings of the independent review of 31 October 2026 (a long PDF review of live build 5bb096 and repository 396d635; decision D43)

tasks.text: **Mastery mixes guided and independent evidence in one posterior** (`app/src/lib/mastery.ts`): cue 1 and 2 successes add weight to `a` and the unlabelled minimum does not stop a large guided history from overwhelming a small independent sample (the reviewer's arithmetic checks out: Beta(56,1) gives 99.9996 percent, Beta(6,1) gives 73.8 percent). Fix: compute the reliability posterior from cue 3+ evidence only; keep guided attempts for the 'practising' state, recommendations and readiness to try a check; wording "demonstrated in independent checks, with counts and dates"; synthetic regression tests (large guided history, repeated families, hints, placement, long inactivity)

**Confidence calibration uses absolute error** (`independence()` in `app/src/lib/progress.ts`), which rewards extreme confidence (verified: true p 0.7 gives expected error 0.42 reporting 0.7 but 0.34 reporting 0.9). Fix: a proper scoring rule, or simply accuracy by confidence band with sample sizes; show high-confidence mistakes as examples

**A fresh-practice set is not strictly independent**: `pickFresh` in `app/src/lib/select.ts` fills short sets with items from already chosen families. Add a strict-family option for checks and allow a shorter check

**Lesson resume by numeric step index** breaks when a rewrite adds or reorders steps. Stable step ids, lesson revision metadata, a restart-or-mapped-place choice after a structural rewrite, the version stored with completion
**Save failures are swallowed** in the lesson player: show a calm notice and an export option instead of a silent success

**First visit waits for the whole lessons file**: split a compact catalogue (titles, outcomes, stages, durations) from lesson bodies, fetch the lesson and its items on demand, separate size budgets for the shell, the first lesson, the optional opponent and the full offline copy; benchmark time to a usable board; content-addressed filenames instead of a hash query string; a missing course catalogue must not look like an empty one

**Lesson roles**: fields for canonical introduction, continuation, course application and assessment, so the map, search and Up next choose the introduction by design (this also fixes the Forks stage-check routing in 2g)
Review scheduling: track historical accomplishment and current evidence separately (a recent failure must not leave a skill "reliable and refreshed"); use the learner's local day for due dates

Practice by purpose (learn with help, retrieve independently, refresh, test a hypothesis) with the result type stored; result vocabulary: correct for this task, sound alternative, useful idea but incomplete calculation, unsuccessful with explanation
Board-first first lesson: a visible board and a meaningful action in the first minute; layered local-storage notice with a backup suggestion after meaningful work

Depth means explanation: readiness = mechanism, conditions, near-miss, unfamiliar use, with step counts as diagnostics only; chapter names and stopping points inside long lessons; prediction only after a worked-example route is offered; transfer checks include positions where the idea does not apply

Maia finale record also keeps the exact start position, assistance settings, content version and whether the game was completed; a beginner invitation passes an explicit gentle default (the play page opens on Stockfish Club today)

Games feeding learning: annotate before the engine; an opportunity log (where the idea could have been used, noticed or not, help, annotation certainty); a short post-game flow (one moment, the original thought, the reply, a possible cause, one follow-up plus a fresh related exercise); recommendations say why

Roadmap truth: replace the single overall percentage with a readiness view (beginner journey, core lesson quality, independent assessment, game integration, accessibility, reliability, human review) generated from the same records that register courses; derive course counts from metadata
(feedback) Evaluation: do not use non-overlapping confidence intervals as the test of change; use a paired analysis and a statistical review before efficacy claims; usability sessions first
Accessibility: real keyboard, screen-reader, narrow-screen and enlarged-text journeys using WCAG 2.2; audio must never play over changed text (version check)

phases.title: Phase 2i: A finishable Foundation with a graduation point (Andrew, 7 November 2026, from an outside review; decision D48)

tasks.text: Tracks: a finite **Foundation** (the required core), optional **Intermediate** and **Advanced** tracks, and an **enrichment library** (opening deep dives, famous games, culture courses, specialist endings). `tools/build_path.py` stops forcing every lesson into one main path: every lesson gets a `track`; the recommended path is the Foundation; the library may keep growing without lengthening the core; the map and lesson list show the track

`docs/foundation.md`: the graduation outcomes, observable, in eight areas: rules and game operation (play a legal game, how it ends, notation, a clock); board awareness and safety; tactics and calculation (common motifs, reject unsound ones, short lines against credible replies); opening play (develop with purpose, king safety, the centre, answer deviations); planning (material, activity, king safety, pawn features, a useful plan in a quiet position); attack and defence; endgames and conversion (queen and rook mates, elementary pawn endings, king activity, converting a clear advantage); independent improvement (review a game before the engine, find a recurring problem, choose practice)

A coverage matrix `tools/foundation_matrix.py` for every required outcome: explained, practised, assessed on fresh tasks, applied in a play-out or game, reviewed by a person; printed and shown in the readiness view; Foundation is "complete" only when every cell is filled

Where the line falls: use stages S0 to S4 as the skeleton, pull the essential S5 material in (pawn weaknesses and breaks, open files, simple exchanges and plans, basic attack conditions and defensive resources, a few model games) and bring simple versions of later ideas forward; leave out of the core: bishop-and-knight mate execution, two-knight theory, queen against rook, detailed Lucena and Philidor (early Intermediate extensions), comprehensive structure courses, every named opening deep dive, the whole famous-games collection, novelty research and tablebase investigations. Decide by outcomes, not by stage number

Missing or too late for a Foundation: an early lesson on winning a won game (you won a piece, now what: king safety, favourable exchanges, restricting counterplay, an ending you can finish; today the conversion lesson is in S6); the elementary opponent-awareness habit early (what does the opponent want, what is their best reply, can I prevent it while improving) before the advanced prophylaxis lessons; "does an idea apply at all" decisions with the first fork and pin lessons, not only in S5; a beginner opening starter package (a White approach, Black replies to 1.e4 and 1.d4, what to do against unfamiliar moves), checked as a coherent sequence
